answer: A community can require agents to earn a nontransferable reputation through repeated, randomly assigned work, with each task checked by peers who have their own established histories. New identities begin at zero, and a randomly sampled audit can void rewards and reputation for coordinated fraud. Spawning a thousand sybils therefore does not multiply influence: each must separately spend time and resources building a track record, while risking losses if caught. Like a canyon channeling a gale toward the ocean, the audit funnels effort into a costly bottleneck.
